incidents.victim: Chainalysis
incidents.vector: An external actor used what the company described as 'offensive agentic techniques' to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools, compounded by a separate on-path attack intercepting user communications.
incidents.impact: Names, usernames, password hashes and live authentication tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed, and some customer accounts on its Know Your Transaction service showed signs of unauthorized access; multiple investigation products were taken offline during remediation.

incidents.victim: Mobile users in Ukraine, the US and Europe (watering-hole visitors)
incidents.vector: Russian state hackers compromised legitimate websites and a Ukrainian web-analytics service (Plerdy), and created spoofed lookalike sites, to deliver device-fingerprinting code and exploit chains to iOS and Android visitors.
incidents.impact: Thousands of mobile users were fingerprinted, with vulnerable devices subjected to exploit chains capable of stealing messages, credentials, photos and other sensitive data; attackers relied on already-patched vulnerabilities rather than zero-days.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — residential proxy network operators
incidents.vector: Staff devices on the White House's dedicated internet address network (AS2650) had consumer residential-proxy SDKs such as Infatica installed, likely bundled with free apps, making the network's IP addresses available for rent.
incidents.impact: At least 28 separate residential-proxy services were found reselling exit access through White House IP addresses over a 30-day period, exposing a sensitive government network to anonymized criminal and fraud traffic.

incidents.victim: 1.3 million+ Android TV set-top boxes and IoT devices worldwide
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — IoT botnet operator (Videostrong Technology Co.)
incidents.vector: China-based device manufacturer Videostrong deliberately embedded the 'XCPE' backdoor in Android TV boxes and other IoT devices, evading Android security review via obfuscation, then sold criminal affiliates access to deploy their own malware modules.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million devices — including telehealth equipment and digital signage — were enrolled in a backdoor network used for ad fraud, residential-proxy resale, screenshot capture and keystroke injection; Google disrupted the infrastructure and banned Videostrong from the Android ecosystem, severing access to an estimated 10 million additional devices.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited leaked Li Auto vehicle identification numbers and expired eSIM numbers tied to Chinese-issued eSender eSIMs to re-register vehicle master accounts.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed EV owners, likely more, were locked out of their vehicles' doors and engines and extorted for roughly $500-$600 to regain access; this is the second such wave after a similar campaign in mid-2025.

incidents.victim: Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 industrial device operators
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-58115, a missing-authentication flaw (CVSS 10.0) in the Node-RED admin interface of Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, to deploy flows that use wget or curl to download a Linux bot.
incidents.impact: Unpatched, internet-exposed industrial controllers were compromised and infected with bot malware despite a vendor patch available since August 2026.

incidents.victim: Amadeus IT Group (affecting Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana Airlines, Singapore Airlines, Malaysia Airlines)
incidents.vector: Attackers used login credentials assigned to a system account to access a vulnerability in a travel booking display environment operated by IT provider Amadeus.
incidents.impact: Booking-display data — including passenger names, flight details, confirmation numbers, and in some cases passports and frequent-flyer numbers — was exposed for well over 190,000 passengers across six airlines; no payment data or airline operational systems were affected.

incidents.victim: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party service provider's platform to gain direct access to the bank's own account and systems.
incidents.impact: Hackers used the bank's own account to transfer an estimated $133 million to other institutions and convert funds into cryptocurrency; some assets have since been frozen and customer accounts were not affected.

incidents.victim: Philippine Overseas Employment Administration
incidents.vector: An unidentified operator used privilege-escalation tools (GodPotato, SeImpersonate) and the Impacket library to access and copy SQL Server backup databases, routed through a Singapore-based staging server.
incidents.impact: Nearly 69GB of data — including overseas-employment case records, contracts, accreditation and cashier/LandBank records — was copied out of agency control within 24 minutes; the stolen data had not yet appeared for sale as of the report.

incidents.victim: European supermarkets, meat suppliers and French national blood banks (refrigeration/cooling systems)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited severe authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in internet-exposed Copeland XWEB supervisory refrigeration controllers, for which a firmware fix had been available since August, to remotely alter temperature settings.
incidents.impact: A second wave of attacks hit supermarkets and food suppliers across a dozen European countries, defrosting refrigerators and freezers and causing tens of millions of dollars in spoiled inventory; cooling units at French national blood banks were also tampered with, prompting a joint CISA/FBI advisory urging critical-infrastructure operators to harden cooling systems.

incidents.victim: UK school estate (multiple affiliated schools)
incidents.vector: A 3AM ransomware affiliate stole backup credentials, created rogue domain-admin accounts, and used living-off-the-land Windows tools to establish trust between separate Active Directory domains and move laterally between schools.
incidents.impact: The attacker exfiltrated data and deployed 3AM ransomware across multiple schools; researchers assessed with moderate confidence that an AI agent handled repetitive command generation and troubleshooting during the intrusion, acting as a force multiplier for the human operator.

incidents.victim: BTCPay Server operators running version 2.4.1 or earlier
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in BTCPay Server 2.4.1 and earlier, fixed in version 2.4.2 released in August 2026, to access and drain hot wallets.
incidents.impact: Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from hot wallets on outdated BTCPay Server instances; BTCPay has urged affected operators to sweep remaining funds, rebuild on fresh servers, and replace exposed credentials.

incidents.victim: Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) users running outdated versions
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 (Synology-SA-24:20) against network storage devices still running outdated DSM versions.
incidents.impact: Outdated Synology NAS devices are being encrypted by ransomware actors; Synology issued a rare public notice urging all users to update DSM immediately and enable automatic updates.

incidents.victim: National Reconnaissance Office / U.S. government classified systems
incidents.vector: A former IT administrator holding a Top Secret clearance at the National Reconnaissance Office used his systems access to remove classified documents from secure U.S. government repositories and hand-carry or electronically transmit them to foreign officials.
incidents.impact: Over roughly two years, the contractor transmitted dozens of Top Secret/SCI documents concerning an active armed conflict to Ethiopian government officials, who used the intelligence in military operations; he pleaded guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information and faces 10-22 years in prison.

incidents.victim: cPGuard customers (cPanel / shared hosting operators)
incidents.vector: An attacker used stolen credentials to access OPSSHIELD's cPGuard update servers and pushed a malicious script through versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.
incidents.impact: The malicious update collected /etc/shadow files, MySQL configuration, root shell history and SSH credentials from affected shared-hosting servers before OPSSHIELD identified and remediated the compromise.

incidents.victim: Mercado Bitcoin
incidents.vector: Unspecified attackers gained access to systems at Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, and stole crypto assets.
incidents.impact: Approximately $49 million in crypto assets were stolen; the company froze about $11 million of the funds and has promised to refund all affected users.

incidents.victim: Michigan State University
incidents.vector: The BYOD ransomware group claims to have breached Michigan State University's network, following a breach the university disclosed the prior month.
incidents.impact: Attackers are threatening to leak personally identifiable data belonging to approximately one million current and former students unless a ransom is paid.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: North Korean operators compromised one Binance engineer via a malicious Homebrew installer delivered through malvertising, then used a fake job-interview process with a malicious coding test to compromise a second engineer's device, ultimately gaining the access needed to control wallet infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Tokens from 11 cryptocurrencies worth $6.3 billion were stolen — the largest cryptocurrency theft in history; Binance recovered or froze roughly $2.8 billion of the stolen stablecoins and has since restored operations, though several billion dollars in Bitcoin and Ethereum remain at large and are being laundered.

incidents.victim: Organizations running internet-facing PAN-OS management interfaces and PHP-based websites globally
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited two critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell'), in some cases chaining them with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access on exposed management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Nearly 70% of websites required emergency patching; government websites across Europe went offline, and a small fraction of internet-facing Palo Alto Networks management interfaces were compromised before patches were applied; CISA, NSA, FBI/IC3 and NYDFS all issued advisories urging immediate patching.

incidents.victim: Space and satellite services, defense/aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: A sophisticated threat actor exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, then installed a custom malware framework dubbed 'KeyDrift' inside SD-WAN control-plane processes.
incidents.impact: The KeyDrift framework provided long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive network keying material; researchers assessed with high confidence that the actor's infrastructure overlaps considerably with a known China-linked covert access network.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Moldovan government networks and began extracting data, which was detected by government IT staff on October 23.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole personal information belonging to roughly one-third of Moldova's population, prompting officials to shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: eMudhra (certificate authority) and downstream TLS-dependent organizations
incidents.vector: A cryptographic defect in eMudhra's certificate-generation process produced intermediate CA private keys with insufficient randomness, allowing the keys to potentially be derived from their public certificates.
incidents.impact: Eight intermediate CA private keys were compromised, creating a risk of forged TLS certificates and meddler-in-the-middle attacks; major browser and OS vendors revoked trust in the affected CAs and eMudhra revoked the certificates, with follow-on remediation advisories issued into November.
